newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria wheat buyers and sellers strike no deals.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria wheat buyers and sellers strike no deals.

text.p: Bulgaria's Sofia Commodity Exchange (SCE) said on Friday the margin between buy and sell wheat prices narrowed and supply topped demand but still no deals were struck at this week's session.

"Buyers bid for 1,590 tonnes of wheat at $136 per tonne ex-works, while sellers offered 3,000 tonnes but were reluctant to sell below $140 per tonne ex-works and no deals were struck," SCE chairman Vasil Simov told a news conference.
One 500 tonne deal tonne deal was struck at $135 per tonne of wheat ex-works at the SCE last week.

"Both buyers and sellers are waiting for the first figures for this year's wheat output but sellers lowered their asking prices to $140 per tonne from $159 last week and we expect deals will soon be struck at the minimum farm gate price set by the cabinet," Simov said.

Bulgaria's cabinet raised grain prices closer to international levels in line with reform pledges to free farm produce trade. The minimum farm gate price was set last month at 230 marks or $135 per tonne of wheat from this year's crop.

Agriculture ministry forecast a wheat output of 2.4 million tonnes in May, but after damage inflicted by hailstorms and heavy rains last month the harvest may be lower, the ministry said three days ago.
Some 32,000 ha planted with wheat and barley and 16,000 ha with spring crops, mainly maize, sunflower and sugar beet, were damaged by the storms last month, ministry data showed.
Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov said in May Bulgaria needed imports of 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat to cover a consumption gap before the 1998 crop.
Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year created acute grain shortages earlier this year. -- Ivan Mastagarkov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
